changes.before: A text-generation model uses a decoder-only Transformer. Is it missing a required separate encoder?
changes.after: A Transformer combines attention with other calculations and information about token positions.

before: A Transformer is a neural-network architecture: a particular way to organize its calculations.
It combines attention with other transformations and information about positions in a sequence. Attention alone is not the entire architecture.
The original Transformer used an encoder and a decoder. An encoder builds representations of input; a decoder produces output from representations.
Encoder-only and decoder-only variants also exist. Many text-generation systems use decoder-style models that generate a continuation.

In causal text generation, a position does not inspect future output tokens that have not been generated. This is a restriction on information access, not a claim about private internals of any current product.
after: An architecture is a design for how parts fit together. A Transformer is one neural-network architecture.
A Transformer combines attention with other calculations and information about positions in a sequence. Attention is one part of the design.
The original Transformer had an encoder and a decoder. The encoder built representations of the input. The decoder used representations to produce output.
Other designs use only encoder-style or decoder-style blocks. A decoder-only Transformer can generate text without a separate encoder.

before.question: A text-generation model uses a decoder-only Transformer. Is it missing a required separate encoder?
choices: Not necessarily. Decoder-only is a valid Transformer variant.
Yes. Every Transformer must have the original two-part layout.
No. A Transformer is just a token counter with no learned parameters.
before.explanation: The architecture family includes different arrangements, not only the original encoder-decoder design.

after.question: A text model uses a decoder-only Transformer. Is a separate encoder required?
choices: No. Decoder-only is a valid Transformer design.
Yes. Every Transformer needs the original two-part design.
No, because Transformers have no learned parameters.
after.explanation: The Transformer family includes encoder-only, decoder-only, and encoder-decoder designs.
